report:
**Conclusion: the claim is true in the United States.** Kyleena is FDA-approved (a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) with the labeled indication to prevent pregnancy **for up to five years**. The FDA-approved prescribing label also directs that it be **replaced after five years** if contraception is to continue.

The duration is supported by its clinical-development evidence: the manufacturer’s reported five-year study found a Kaplan–Meier cumulative pregnancy rate of **1.45%** (13 pregnancies), with a first-year Pearl Index of **0.16**. These figures support high effectiveness during the labeled five-year period; they do not establish that the same device should be relied on beyond five years.

“Up to five years” does not mean it protects against sexually transmitted infections, and it can be removed earlier by a clinician. Individual suitability and risks (including pregnancy with an IUD in place) should be discussed with a healthcare professional.

Sources:  
- FDA-approved label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf  
- U.S. National Library of Medicine drug label: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080  
- Clinical efficacy summary: https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy
